limitations_and_boundaries: Only male mice were studied; findings may not generalize to females.
C3 KO is a global knockout; cell-type-specific roles of C3 are not addressed.
The study does not directly demonstrate that C3-mediated synapse loss causes cognitive decline, only correlation.
Mechanism of C3 action (e.g., microglial phagocytosis) is inferred but not directly tested in aging context.
Sample sizes for some experiments (e.g., Golgi, electrophysiology) are small.
C3 mRNA levels did not show consistent age-related increase, contrasting with protein data.
The study does not examine other complement components or pathways.
Findings are limited to C57BL/6J background; strain-specific effects possible.
Rescue experiments (e.g., C3 re-expression) were not performed to confirm causality.
Behavioral tests were limited to a few tasks; broader cognitive domains not assessed.
